newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE looking at Eurofighter - industry sources.
newsitem.headline: UAE looking at Eurofighter - industry sources.

text.p: The UAE has recently looked at the Eurofighter and its makers are awaiting word on whether the Gulf Arab state will consider the aircraft for a key deal worth up to $6 billion, industry sources said on Monday.
"People from the United Arab Emirates in recent weeks went to England and looked at the Eurofighter programme," an industry source told Reuters.
"British Aerospace (and its Eurofighter partners) at this point are waiting to see what the UAE decides. They are awaiting their response," another industry source said.
Eurofighter partners are British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), Alenia Spa of Italy and Spain's CASA. Alenia is a unit of state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica.
The UAE is looking for up to 80 long-range strike aircraft in a deal potentially worth $6 billion.

The Eurofighter partners had originally bid for the deal, with an offer to lease Tornado aircraft ahead of the development of the Eurofighter 2000. But last year official UAE military sources said U.S. firm Lockheed Martin Corp and France's Dassault Aviation were the only two serious contenders.
